summary: Shinpei Ogura was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1903 to 1906. He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (circa 1926–1933) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1933–1943), where he succeeded Katsuji Fujioka in 1933.

Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo from around 1934 to 1959, and served as professor at Toyo University and Kokugakuin University.

Shintaro Kitano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He held posts as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and as a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).

Shintei Hinonishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shigeru Gorai. He held academic posts at Koyasan University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and later as a professor (attested 2008).
Shinten Sakai worked in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teacher Shindo Shiraishi and held an academic post at Koyasan University, attested in 1959.

Shinya Moriyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo, the University of Vienna, and under Eli Franco in 2002. He held a teaching post at Shinshu University around 2008.

Shinya Yasutomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Otani University. He held multiple academic posts at Otani University, including professor (~1991–2010), and directed the Shinshu Otani-ha Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies (~2008–2014).

Shiro Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Komazawa University, Waseda University, the University of Tokyo, and under Zuiho Yamaguchi and Yasuaki Nara. He was an assistant and later professor at Komazawa University (1995–2020).

Shivram Dattatray Joshi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Śaṅkarśāstri Mārulkar, Maheshvarshastri Joshi, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard. He served as professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University and headed the Sanskrit Dictionary Department at Deccan College.

Shizuka Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, Bukkyo University, and under Jikidō Takasaki. In 1990 he joined Hanazono University, becoming an assistant professor in 1992 and professor in 2002.
Shizuka Shirakawa was a scholar of sinology and linguistics. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from around 1938 to 1943 and later held a post there from circa 1954 to 1981.

Shlomo Pines was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as a lecturer at the University of Paris (1937–1939) and professor of philosophy at the Hebrew University (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1920–1923) and the University of Königsberg (~1923–1924), and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from circa 1928 to 1970.

Shobha Rani Dash works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was an open-recruitment researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010, a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012), and a professor at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1978 to 1987 under Shoko Takeuchi. He held an affiliation as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University, attested between 1995 and 2013.

Shodo Harada is a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Shofuku-ji and under Mumon Yamada (1962–1982), whom he succeeded. He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sōgenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

Shodo Yamagami is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University between 1958 and 1964 and served as an assistant professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from circa 1972 to 2009.

Shogo Watanabe is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (circa 1973–1983). He held posts at Toyo University from around 1988 to 2021, serving as professor from circa 2002 to 2021.

Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies specialist who studied at Komazawa University and under Kōshō Uchiyama. He held positions at Pioneer Valley Zendo, Kyoto Soto Zen Center, Minnesota Zen Meditation Center, and directed the Sōtō Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).

Shoichi Ozawa was a scholar in Japanology and history and archaeology. He completed his studies at Waseda University between circa 1950 and 1954, and later held a post at the Open University of Japan.
